claim: The RQ-Bench study states in its introduction that LLMs are now used not only to generate scientific ideas, but also to judge them.
quote: LLMs are now used not only to generate scientific ideas, but also to judge them.

claim: The same study notes that if LLMs generate a scientific artifact and other LLMs judge its novelty, the whole pipeline depends on whether LLM-as-judge is reliable.
quote: If LLMs generate a scientific artifact and other LLMs judge its novelty, the whole pipeline depends on whether LLM-as-judge is reliable.

claim: CORE-Bench asks whether AI agents can automate computational reproducibility of published scientific research.
quote: In this paper, we ask: Can AI agents automate computational reproducibility of published scientific research?

claim: The CORE-Bench authors decide that an agent solves a task correctly if its reported results for all questions fall within a 95% prediction interval of the results from three manual runs.
quote: We determine if an agent correctly solves a task if the agent's reported results for all questions fall within a 95% prediction interval for every task question of the results from the three manual runs

claim: The CORE-Bench authors suggest that building the benchmark on public repositories enables periodic updates, which could mitigate concerns about contamination and saturation.
quote: CORE-Bench's foundation in public repositories enables periodic updates of the benchmark tasks, which could mitigate concerns about contamination and saturation.

claim: PaperBench develops rubrics that hierarchically decompose each replication task into smaller sub-tasks with clear grading criteria.
quote: For objective evaluation, we develop rubrics that hierarchically decompose each replication task into smaller sub-tasks with clear grading criteria.

claim: The PaperBench authors report that, given the complexity of ML research papers, grading a single replication attempt can take tens of hours for a human expert.
quote: Given the complexity of ML research papers, we found that even grading a single replication attempt can take tens of hours for a human expert.

claim: The survey on benchmark data contamination defines it as occurring when language models inadvertently incorporate evaluation benchmark information from their training data.
quote: However, it has also resulted in a significant issue known as Benchmark Data Contamination (BDC). This occurs when language models inadvertently incorporate evaluation benchmark information from their training data, leading to inaccurate or unreliable performance during the evaluation phase of the process.

claim: A clinical-agent study observes that benchmarks typically score one run per task and rarely ask whether identical inputs produce identical actions.
quote: benchmarks typically score one run per task and rarely ask whether identical inputs produce identical actions

claim: CORE-Bench judges a task correct only if the agent's reported results for all questions fall within a 95% prediction interval of three manual runs.
quote: We determine if an agent correctly solves a task if the agent's reported results for all questions fall within a 95% prediction interval for every task question of the results from the three manual runs (although only 17 / 181 task questions have stochastic answers).

claim: The CORE-Bench authors say that building the benchmark on public repositories enables periodic updates that could mitigate concerns about contamination and saturation.
quote: CORE-Bench's foundation in public repositories enables periodic updates of the benchmark tasks, which could mitigate concerns about contamination and saturation.

claim: A later case study of CORE-Bench Hard reports surfacing threats to construct validity that were difficult to anticipate with less capable agents.
quote: First, we surface threats to construct validity in CORE-Bench Hard that are difficult to anticipate with less capable agents.

claim: The PaperBench authors report that expert human grading took on the order of tens of hours per paper, which motivated the automated judge.
quote: In preliminary experiments, we found that manual grading using expert humans took on the order of tens of hours per paper, so having an automated way to perform the evaluation is necessary for the practical application of PaperBench.

claim: PaperBench also reports high variance on the same paper for most agents and recommends several seeds.
quote: Notably, for most agents, we see high variance in results on the same paper. Due to the high variance, we recommend others to use several seeds when evaluating PaperBench to get an accurate measure of agent performance.

claim: SciReplicate-Bench instead prioritizes execution accuracy, and its authors criticize PaperBench-style approaches for relying on manual criteria and LLM judgments.
quote: This represents a unique challenge at the intersection of scientific literature comprehension and executable code synthesis. While recent parallel efforts such as PaperBench (Starace et al., 2025) and Paper2CodeBench (Seo et al., 2025) have tackled related problems by exploring full codebase reconstruction, these evaluation approaches rely substantially on manual assessment criteria and LLM-based correctness judgments, introducing potential inconsistencies and reliability concerns. Our approach prioritizes objective evaluation through execution accuracy, providing more rigorous validation than non-executable assessment methodologies (Wang et al., 2022;Chen et al., 2021).
locator: sec. Our work makes the following contributions:, para 5

claim: SciReplicate-Bench chose a 2024 publication window to minimize the risk of data leakage.
quote: It consists of 100 code reproduction tasks derived from 36 papers published in leading conferences in 2024. This recent publication window was deliberately chosen to minimize the risk of data leakage.

claim: PaperBench's authors report that their best LLM-based judge, which uses o3-mini-high with custom scaffolding, achieves an F1 score of 0.83 on the auxiliary evaluation, suggesting it is a reasonable stand-in for a human judge.
quote: Our best LLM-based judge, which uses o3-mini-high with custom scaffolding, achieves an F1 score of 0.83 on the auxiliary evaluation, suggesting that this judge is a reasonable stand-in for a human judge.

claim: The PaperBench authors state that more work is needed to improve judge accuracy and understand judges' strengths and weaknesses.
quote: We've taken an early step with JudgeEval (Section 4.2) to measure the accuracy of model-based judges on tasks with huge complex outputs, but more work is needed to improve accuracy and understand their strengths and weaknesses.
locator: sec. A.2. Improving automated judges, para 104

claim: A large-scale evaluation found that judge validation relying on exact-match agreement does not correct for chance and systematically overstates discriminative ability.
quote: judge validation in practice relies on exact-match agreement, a metric that does not correct for chance and systematically overstates discriminative ability.

claim: A controlled study of novelty judges found that telling the judge that reviewers found one idea novel and the other not can change its verdict on more than half of identical idea pairs.
quote: simply telling the judge that reviewers found one idea novel and the other not can change its verdict on more than half of the identical idea pairs it is shown, shifting pairwise accuracy by over 50 points and occasionally pushing it below chance.

claim: HindSight reports that its scores are negatively correlated with LLM-judged novelty.
quote: Moreover, HindSight scores are \emph{negatively} correlated with LLM-judged novelty ($ρ{=}{-}0.29$, $p{<}0.01$), suggesting that LLMs systematically overvalue novel-sounding ideas that never materialize in real research.

claim: PaperBench pairs each paper with manually created rubrics that specify the outcomes needed for replication.
quote: Each paper is accompanied by a manually created rubric, which specifies all the necessary outcomes for replicating the paper in detail; resulting in a total of 8,316 individually gradable outcomes across 20 papers.

claim: PaperBench rubrics are hierarchical, so that partial progress toward replication can be measured at a fine grain.
quote: Rubrics are constructed in a hierarchical manner, such that outcomes can be decomposed into finegrained sub-outcomes, allowing granular measurement of partial progress towards replicating papers.

quote: Our best LLM-based judge, which uses o3-mini-high with custom scaffolding, achieves an F1 score of 0.83 on the auxiliary evaluation

claim: A survey of agentic evaluation papers reports that about 82% of its sample use structurally mismatched, incomplete, or absent inter-rater reliability metrics.
quote: We examine the model's predictions against a structured survey of 55 published agentic evaluation papers, finding that approximately 82% of papers in this purposive sample apply structurally mismatched, incomplete, or absent inter-rater reliability (IRR) metrics, a pattern consistent with systematic $V_3$ collapse.

claim: The TRUCE authors state that the majority of open source benchmarks available today have been contaminated or leaked into LLMs.
quote: However, recent work has pointed out that the majority of the open source benchmarks available today have been contaminated or leaked into LLMs, meaning that LLMs have access to test data during pretraining and/or fine-tuning.

claim: The rephrased-samples study reports that simple variations of test data, such as paraphrasing and translation, can bypass n-gram decontamination.
quote: While most data decontamination efforts apply string matching (e.g., n-gram overlap) to remove benchmark data, we show that these methods are insufficient, and simple variations of test data (e.g., paraphrasing, translation) can easily bypass these decontamination measures.

claim: SciReplicate-Bench selected papers published in 2024 with public code repositories to mitigate the risk of data leakage.
quote: To mitigate the risk of data leakage, we selected papers published in 2024 that provide publicly available code repositories.

claim: ResearchBench states that, to prevent data contamination, it focuses exclusively on publications from 2024 onward, which it says ensures minimal overlap with LLM pretraining data.
quote: To prevent data contamination, we focus exclusively on publications from 2024 onward, ensuring minimal overlap with LLM pretraining data;

quote: CORE-Bench's foundation in public repositories enables periodic updates of the benchmark tasks, which could mitigate concerns about contamination and saturation.

claim: The tabular-data study finds that LLMs perform better on datasets seen during training, indicating that memorization leads to overfitting.
quote: We find that LLMs perform better on datasets seen during training, indicating that memorization leads to overfitting.

claim: TRUCE proposes keeping test datasets private and evaluating models without revealing the test data to the model.
quote: To solve this problem, we propose Private Benchmarking, a solution where test datasets are kept private and models are evaluated without revealing the test data to the model.

claim: PaperBench reports that for most agents there is high variance in results on the same paper, and its authors recommend using several seeds when evaluating.
quote: Notably, for most agents, we see high variance in results on the same paper. Due to the high variance, we recommend others to use several seeds when evaluating PaperBench to get an accurate measure of agent performance.

claim: FIRE-Bench reports that even its strongest agents achieve limited rediscovery success and exhibit high variance across runs.
quote: Our results show that full-cycle scientific research remains challenging for current agent systems: even the strongest agents achieve limited rediscovery success (<50 F1), exhibit high variance across runs, and display recurring failure modes in experimental design, execution, and evidence-based reasoning.

claim: The same study concludes that single-trial LLM judging is often too noisy for high-stakes evaluation.
quote: A reliability curve analysis shows that, in our dataset, 11 repeated trials are needed for a majority vote to recover the 50-trial reference verdict with 95% probability on average, rising to 15 for high-variance questions. These findings suggest that single-trial LLM judging is often too noisy for high-stakes evaluation, and that multi-trial aggregation, position randomization, and explicit uncertainty reporting should be standard practice.

claim: In a clinical agent benchmark, a rerun study found that the benchmark reports the same failing verdict for materially different behaviour in 22 of 43 divergent groups.
quote: In 22 of those 43 the benchmark reports the same failing verdict for materially different behaviour, as it does for all 10 divergent groups of the 4B model at 0.7.

claim: The human study with over 100 NLP researchers reports that LLM-generated ideas were judged more novel than human expert ideas while being judged slightly weaker on feasibility.
quote: we find LLM-generated ideas are judged as more novel (p < 0.05) than human expert ideas while being judged slightly weaker on feasibility.

claim: The same study acknowledges that human novelty judgments are hard.
quote: Finally, we acknowledge that human judgements of novelty can be difficult, even by experts, and propose an end-to-end study design which recruits researchers to execute these ideas into full projects, enabling us to study whether these novelty and feasibility judgements result in meaningful differences in research outcome.

claim: RQ-Bench reports that LLM judges rate model-generated research questions as highly novel, a pattern its authors call a novelty mirage.
quote: LLM judges consistently rate model-generated RQs as highly novel, producing a novelty mirage; in comparative evaluations, this preference becomes even stronger.

claim: A study of novelty-judge design found that simply telling the judge that reviewers found one idea novel and the other not can change its verdict on more than half of the identical idea pairs it is shown, shifting pairwise accuracy by over 50 points and occasionally pushing it below chance.
quote: simply telling the judge that reviewers found one idea novel and the other not can change its verdict on more than half of the identical idea pairs it is shown, shifting pairwise accuracy by over 50 points and occasionally pushing it below chance.

claim: The study of novelty-judge design reported that retrieval and larger reasoning budgets help little, and that two purpose-built novelty evaluators are outperformed by its cheapest prompted baseline.
quote: Retrieval and larger reasoning budgets help little, and two purpose-built novelty evaluators are outperformed by our cheapest prompted baseline.

claim: OpenNovelty takes a grounding approach, tying novelty assessments to retrieved real papers.
quote: Unlike naive LLM-based approaches, \textsc{OpenNovelty} grounds all assessments in retrieved real papers, ensuring verifiable judgments.
